# A program's func or const named like a property the browser's window holds
# as its own -- `closed`, `top`, `status` -- reaches a test on html. The page
# put each name a test may read on window, and `closed` and `top` have only a
# getter there, so the page raised as it booted; `status` took the value as a
# string. Those go on window.__snglOwn, which the test module reads them
# from (javascript.WindowOwn).

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

const status list[int] = [5, 6]

func closed(n int) int {
    return n + 1
}

func top(n int) int {
    return n + 2
}

func name(n int) int {
    return n + 3
}

component page ui.node {
    var n = 1

    ui.text("{closed(n)} {top(n)} {name(n)}")
}

func testAFuncNamedLikeAWindowProperty(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(closed(c.n) == 2 && top(c.n) == 3 && name(c.n) == 4)
    var f = closed
    var g = top
    t.assert(f(c.n) == 2 && g(c.n) == 3)
    t.assert(status[c.n] == 6)
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
-- testrun/html/none/app.sngl/page/1 --
sha256:0b3aa664bc3caf7194f1e3d03c89dd62

  "results": [
    {
      "Desc": "AFuncNamedLikeAWindowProperty",
      "Passed": true
    }
  ]
}
